title: validation-first rolling pivot for private control-plane upgrades
creator: Anita Patel
description:
Goal: implement an automated, validation-first rolling upgrade process for Private (VPC) control planes that uses Terraform/IaC modules and tightly-scoped canary cohorts to reduce blast radius and enable safe rollbacks.

Scope: Terraform module extensions, preflight validation suite, phased canary orchestration, runtime compatibility checks (KV cache & API schema), automated health gates and observability hooks. This ticket covers the design and initial automation to run a controlled pivot of control plane components (operator + control plane API) between versions in customer VPCs.

Design overview and requirements:
- Use dedicated Terraform 'upgrade' modules that produce a plan artifact and a staged apply path: plan -> apply-canary-1 -> monitor -> apply-canary-2 -> apply-all. Keep modules idempotent and add a 'preview-only' mode.
- Validation-first approach: run preflight validators (schema compatibility, CRD compatibility, operator binary compatibility, DB migration dry-run) before any apply. Validators run as ephemeral jobs in a customer-like staging account.
- Canary cohorts: target 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% of control planes within a rollout pool. Cohorts defined by tags (region, tenant size, SLA tier).
- Health gates: define SLOs and thresholds for gating: p95 API latency, reconciliation error rate, controller restarts, control-plane API 5xx rate, and critical reconciliation lag. Fail gates trigger automated rollback and alerting.
- Automated rollback: capture and store Terraform plan outputs + state snapshots before each cohort apply. On gate failure, run a 'revert' path that re-applies the previously recorded state and triggers post-rollback validations.
- Observability & tracing: emit candidate-version metrics (version tag) and expose canary cohort dashboards for quick slice analysis. Add tracing sampling for upgrade windows.
- Safety: require signed approvals for the 50% and 100% cohort steps; small cohorts can proceed automatically if gates pass.
- Compatibility checks: KV cache serialization compatibility tests, persisted cache migration checks, model runtime kernel compatibility checks (for customers with dedicated GPUs), and storage migration dry-runs.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Infra + IaC primitives (2 sprints): terraform module for canary apply, plan artifact storage (S3), state snapshot hooks, pipeline templates.
2) Validator suite (1 sprint): implement schema/CRD dry-run, operator compatibility test harness, DB migration simulator.
3) Orchestration + gating (2 sprints): pipeline steps, cohort manager, gating metrics wiring to console dashboards.
4) Pilot rollouts (1 sprint): run on internal test VPCs, then opt-in customers. Collect runbook and audit logs.

Success criteria:
- Automated canary can complete 1%->10% step without manual intervention in 95% of runs during pilot.
- All preflight validators run in <12 minutes for typical control plane sizes.
- Rollback restores previous state within target RTO of 20 minutes for pilot customers.
- Monitoring dashboards surface per-cohort errors with 1-minute freshness.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/PCP-Upgrade-Automation
- Terraform modules RFC: drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XUpg-terraform-upgrades
- GH PR (IaC prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1984
- Validator harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane-validations
- Console dashboard mock: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/upgrade-cohorts

Open decisions and trade-offs:
- Whether to default to traffic-shadowing (zero-downtime shadow traffic) vs. in-place operator replacement. Traffic-shadowing reduces blast radius but doubles resource usage during windows. Initial plan favors in-place with a shadow option for elite customers.
- How much of orchestration to expose to customers vs keep fully-managed. We will implement a managed default and a customer opt-in path via Terraform variables.
- Level of automatic rollback aggressiveness (strict vs tolerant). Start strict for first two releases, then loosen if noise is low.

Next steps:

- Prototype preflight CRD dry-run in validator harness (owner: Priya Rao).
- Add audit hooks to state snapshots (owner: Security team contact: Jorge Mendes).
